html:
SMTO-EXE-0002 — Privileged environment unsupported

GUID: e6ba61b8-fcc9-457e-ab41-381cc23eed1f
Slug: privileged-environment-unsupported
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to run a command with administrator rights along with extra custom settings, and it only allows its own built-in settings for such commands. The command did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to run the administrator command without setting extra environment variables, and to put any needed values directly in the command. Only SMTO's own built-in settings can be passed to commands that run with administrator rights.
  2. If the command needs a password or token, let SMTO ask you for it when it runs instead of putting it in a setting. SMTO has a separate, private way to collect administrator passwords.
  3. If the command doesn't really need administrator rights, ask SMTO to run it normally. Commands without administrator rights can use your custom settings.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and its output appears in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer; the details name the settings that were refused. Don't send the same request unchanged, because it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused an elevated (sudo/administrator) command because its environment bindings included names outside SMTO's permitted run and activity metadata (for example OF_RUN_ID, OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR, TMPDIR, TEMP) or names with invalid syntax; the command was not executed.

What this means

  • Privileged dispatch found environment names outside its permitted runtime-metadata set or invalid environment-name syntax before launching the elevated command. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Privileged dispatch found environment names outside its permitted runtime-metadata set or invalid environment-name syntax before launching the elevated command.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the supplied names with the privilege route's supported metadata bindings; keep credential values in the private elevation flow.

How to fix it

  • Remove the unsupported variables named in the message from the privileged request's env, passing needed values as command arguments instead, and let the supported privilege credential flow supply any password. Resubmit only after the bindings are limited to SMTO's run/activity metadata names (see PRIVILEGED_RUNTIME_METADATA_KEYS in src/gateway_core/privilege.py).
  • Correct the environment bindings before retrying; use the supported privilege credential flow for elevation values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Only supported valid bindings reach the privileged launcher, and any resulting execution receipt is checked.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
